sources.access_method: Direct API fetch, HTTP 200, JSON parsed
sources.what_it_supported: Recall campaign counts by model year for Tesla Model Y (2020-2025): 24, 23, 20, 17, 5, 3. Individual recall components including suspension knuckle fracture (2020-2022), front suspension lateral link fasteners (2020-2021), seat belt fasteners (2019-2021), brake caliper bolts (2020-2021), second-row seat back bolts (2022-2023), steering wheel fastener (2022-2023), pyrotechnic battery disconnect (2023), TPMS (2020-2025), AP4 computer short/camera blackout (2023-2025), certification label (2025-2026).
sources.notes: Authoritative US government data. Free VIN-level lookup at https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls

sources.access_method: Full page text retrieved via r.jina.ai reader proxy, HTTP 200
sources.what_it_supported: Reliability scores by year (2020: 46, 2021: 46, 2022: 50, 2023: 53, 2024: 63, 2025: 70); 83 recalls / 3,358 complaints aggregate; complaint-category counts (forward collision avoidance 875, acceleration/cruise 434, electrical 335, steering 333); heat pump repair quote floor of $3,000 on a 2021; main computer quote ~$2,300; 48.4% value retention at 5 years; 2020 and 2021 identified as weakest years, 2024 as best used pick.
sources.notes: Aggregates NHTSA complaint data with its own scoring methodology. Used here for complaint-category ranking and repair-cost ballparks, not as a verdict.

sources.access_method: Tesla blocks direct fetch (HTTP 403 through proxy). Terms confirmed via search-result snippets of the official page, corroborated across independent secondary sources describing the same 8-year / 100k-150k / 70% structure.
sources.what_it_supported: Basic vehicle warranty 4 yr / 50,000 mi. Battery and drive unit 8 years with mileage caps of 100,000 / 120,000 / 150,000 depending on model and configuration, plus 70% minimum capacity retention. Emissions Performance Warranty covers charge-related HV components on Model 3 and Model Y.
sources.notes: Model Y specifically: 8 yr / 120,000 mi for Long Range and Performance; 8 yr / 100,000 mi for Standard Range. Confirm against the warranty booklet for the specific VIN.

sources.access_method: Corroborated across multiple independent search snippets describing an identical menu path and software version
sources.what_it_supported: In-car Battery Health Test path is Controls > Service > Battery Health, available after software update 2025.8.4; runs 15-20 minutes; requires the car parked and plugged into AC power; compares measured capacity to expected energy retention for pack type, age and usage. Tesla app alternative: Service > Battery & Range.
sources.notes: Fallback for older software: Controls > Software > long-press the model badge ~3 seconds > type 'service' to enter Service Mode.

sources.access_method: Search-result snippet, corroborated by drivequip.com and poweringautos.com summaries
sources.what_it_supported: Remaining original battery and drive-unit warranty generally follows the vehicle to subsequent owners; damage, misuse and modifications may not qualify; degradation above the retention threshold is not a claim.
sources.notes: Consistent with Tesla's own language that coverage transfers to subsequent owners.

excluded_or_unverified: No firm 2026 used-market price ranges were included. The 48.4% five-year residual figure is the only pricing data point used, and it is attributed to its source.
Battery pack replacement cost was deliberately left qualitative. Widely-cited figures vary too much by pack condition and refurbishment to present as fact.
Recurrent Auto's used-Tesla buying guide returned HTTP 404 and was not used.
